aliases.name: APS
aliases.note: From the Russian abbreviation for Stechkin automatic pistol.

massEmpty.sourceNote: 1.22 kg. The article does not say whether the wooden holster-stock is included; the figure is roughly twice a Makarov pistol's.

length.sourceNote: Pistol alone, without the holster-stock attached.

cyclicRate.sourceNote: 750 rounds a minute, published as a single figure rather than a range. It is the rate the pistol's rate-reducer mechanism exists to produce.

effectiveRange.sourceNote: Effective range as published. The same source gives a maximum range of 200 m, which is also the furthest setting on the rear sight.

sightGraduation.sourceNote: The rear sight is a rotating drum with settings at 25, 50, 100 and 200 m.

capacity.sourceNote: 20-round double-column steel box magazine with a two-position feed.

images.alt: A blued Soviet pistol lying on a plywood bench, seen from the left at an angle. It is unusually long-slided for a pistol, with a chequered brown grip, a slide-mounted selector lever and a large box magazine standing proud of the butt. Attached to the rear of the grip is a hollow wooden holster used as a shoulder stock, longer than the pistol itself.
images.caption: A Stechkin APS with its wooden holster clipped to the butt as a shoulder stock. The lever on the slide is the combined safety, decocker and fire selector; the arsenal mark and year are stamped on the frame above the trigger.

images.alt: A police officer in woodland camouflage, body armour and a green helmet with a clear visor, firing a black Stechkin pistol two-handed inside a wooden indoor range. The pistol is held without its stock.
images.caption: An officer of the Moscow OMON firing an APS on an indoor range. The pistol is being used here as a pistol, with the holster-stock left off, which is how it was carried in police service.
